His question: if AI solves the hardest math, why are companies so far behind? His main answer: context.
Intro · What context is
Context is everything the model sees
A model answers from two things: what it learned in training, and what is in front of it right now. The second one is context.
Your prompt
The question or the task you type.
The conversation
Everything said earlier in the same chat.
Instructions and files
What is loaded before you type a word.
What tools bring back
A search result, a CRM record, a doc it opened.
It all lands in one place, the context window, and the model reads it fresh on every answer. It remembers nothing else about you.
Intro · Why it matters
The model knows the world. It does not know you.
From training · the same for everyone
How to write a cold email
Sales and marketing practice in general
Public facts, up to its cut-off date
Only from context · yours alone
Why your customers bought
What your reps heard on calls this week
Your prices, your voice, where you lose
Leave the right side empty and the model fills it with the average of everyone else.
?

A concrete example
Inside icp.md
Six headings. Each one answers a question you get asked every week.
The second heading matters most: saying who you do not sell to stops the AI from writing to everyone.
“Their words” changes output the most. The model starts writing in the buyer’s language.
gtm-context/icp.md
## Who we sell to Type, size range and why, tools they use ## Who we do not sell to Red flags, deals we lost or regret, and why ## The buyer Title, who else signs, what they fear ## Triggers Events that make them look now ## Their words 5 quotes from calls, verbatim, with source ## Last reviewed Date, by whom, from which calls
A second example
Inside a battle card
One card per competitor, one to two pages.
“Why we lose” is the part teams skip. Without it the AI oversells, and the buyer notices.
A landmine is a question that lets the buyer find the competitor’s gap themselves.
Sections adapted from Klue, Competitive battlecards 101
gtm-context/competitors/acme.md
## Quick dismiss One line for when their name comes up ## Why we win 3 reasons, each with the proof to show ## Why we lose Honest, with the deals behind it ## Landmines Questions that expose their gap ## Objections What they say about us, and our answer ## Last reviewed Date, by whom, their latest price change
The format
Why plain markdown
Write for the agent first, then for people. Markdown is the one format both can read.
Every tool reads it
Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and every agent index file use it.
Changes are tracked
In git you see who changed which line, when and why.
Anyone can fix it
A rep who spots a wrong line edits it in any text editor.
It travels
Push it to other systems by API or MCP, or paste it.
Anthropic: sections with “XML tagging or Markdown headers” · OpenAI: JSON did poorly in long-context tests · Microsoft 365 Copilot uploads do not list .md: keep a .txt or .docx copy
The format · Agents first, people too
One repo, two readers
1
A change to a file is proposed and approved in Git.
2
Agents read the new .md file straight away.
3
A site builder turns the same files into pages for people. Nobody publishes by hand.
Keep the site private. It says where you lose.
context.yourcompany.com · rebuilt on every merge

The format · One file or many
Several small files, one index
200
lines for the index
The file that is always loaded. Past that, the model follows it less.

1
page each, today
Our rule for this afternoon: one topic per file, one page per topic.
Why small: across 18 models, accuracy fell as the input got longer (Chroma, Context Rot, 2025) · limits from Anthropic memory docs, Agent Skills best practices and Cursor rules

Quality bar
Specific, sourced, short, honest, current
The test for every line: could a competitor paste it into their own file?
Specific
“Owner of 2 to 5 sites who books by phone” beats “SMB”.
Sourced
Each claim names the call, deal or doc behind it.
Short
One page per file. Long files get followed less.
Honest
Where you lose, who is a bad fit, what you never claim.
Current
A date and an owner on each file. Stale is worse than none.
How you build it
You do not write it by hand
The knowledge already exists in your documents. You talk to an AI that turns it into the layer.
Your existing docs
Website, decks, about 15 call transcripts
The AI reads, then interviews you
One question at a time
It drafts the files
Every claim with its source
You edit
Cut, correct, approve
Your job is to answer and correct, not to type. The interview is where what lives in your head gets in.
A prompt to start from
The builder prompt
paste into Claude Code or Codex
You are building my GTM context layer. Read every file in ./sources: decks, docs, call transcripts. Then interview me, one question at a time, about what is missing or contradictory. Stop after ten questions. Write gtm-context/icp.md and gtm-context/positioning.md. Rules - Quote buyers word for word and name the source of each claim. - When two documents disagree, show me both and ask which is true. - Say who we do not sell to, and what we never claim. - One page per file. Mark anything you guessed as [TO CONFIRM]. - End each file with: last reviewed, date, sources used.

Exercise
25 min
Build two files
1
Fill a sources folder: your deck or website text, and 2 to 5 call transcripts. Add an empty gtm-context folder.
2
Paste the builder prompt into Claude Code or Codex. No coding tool? Upload the sources to a Claude or ChatGPT project.

Where it lives
One folder, every tool points to it
Pick the home your team will open. Two copies means one of them is wrong.
A git repository
History and review built in. Claude Code and Codex read it directly.
A shared drive folder
Fine to start with. No review step, so name one owner per file.
A GTM platform
Vasco, for example, keeps the files next to your live CRM data.
A skills library
Claude Code and Codex load skills: SKILL.md folders kept in the same repo.
The home · Git
Why a Git repository
A folder with a memory: every change is recorded, proposed and approved.
Full history
Who changed which line, when and why. Any version can be restored.
Review before change
An edit is a proposal. The file’s owner approves it first.
One source
People and tools read the same files. No stray copy in someone’s drive.
Agents work in it
Claude Code and Codex read it, edit it and propose changes.
Who works this way: GitLab runs its company handbook on merge requests · open examples to browse: getnao/sylph, anthropics/skills
The home · How a change gets in
First a proposal, then a fact
1
A rep spots a line that is no longer true.
2
They tell the AI to fix it, or edit the file on github.com.
3
The change appears as a pull request: old line, new line.
4
The file’s owner approves. Every tool now reads the new line.
pull request · gtm-context/icp.md
## Who we sell to
- Small and mid-size gyms
+ Owners of 2 to 5 sites who still book by phone
+ Source: 6 discovery calls, Nov 2026
Proposed by a rep · approved by the ICP owner
You do not need to learn the Git commands. Ask the AI to “open a pull request with this change”; your part is to read the two lines and say yes or no.
The home · Plugging it in
How each tool reads the repo
Claude Code, Codex
Open the folder. They read AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md first.
Claude Projects
GitHub connector: pick the folder, click “Sync now” after a change.
Claude Team
An owner connects the repo once. Everyone gets each update.
ChatGPT
GitHub app in Settings. It reads the files; Codex writes.
Gemini
Import the repo by its link. A snapshot: import again to refresh.
Docs: Claude GitHub connector · Claude organization sync · ChatGPT GitHub app · Gemini import · checked Nov 2026
The home · Being honest about Git
Start simple. Move when it hurts
This week
A shared folder
The same markdown files in Drive or on your laptop. Name one owner per file.
Move to Git when
Two people edit, or an agent writes
That is when you need history and an approval step.
Never in the repo
Secrets and personal data
No passwords, API keys, contracts or customer contact details.
What kills a context layer is not the tool. It is that nobody keeps it current. That is part 2.

Part 02
The feedback loop
Keep the files true with calls and closed deals.
Why a loop
Context goes stale the day you write it
Calls and closed deals propose changes. The file’s owner approves them.
1 · Collect
calls and deals
2 · Compare
against the files
3 · Propose
a diff + the quote
4 · Approve
the owner merges
Weekly
Why a loop · The evidence
Most company brains die on upkeep
55%
of home-built company brains were abandoned
Almost always on upkeep, not on technology.
1 in 5
teams say theirs works
Another 24% tried and gave up.
78%
trust a doc that a named person verified
Ahead of a link to a live source (63%) and a recent date (56%).
Slite, company brain survey, 149 AI-forward teams, July 2026. A vendor survey with a self-selected sample: read it as a signal, not a census.

The loop · Where a new fact goes first
Evidence first, conclusions second
record/
A log you only add to: date, source, quote.
gtm-context/
The six files. Rewritten when the log says so.
Three separate mentions before a line in a file changes. One loud prospect is a log entry, not a rule.
record/2026-11.md
2026-11-18 · call · lost deal “It has to work with our door system.” > objection: door access · mention 2 2026-11-20 · call · won deal “We were live in three weeks.” > proof: onboarding speed · mention 4
Pattern from GTMnow (a context folder you rewrite, a record folder you only add to) and Jacob Dietle (every claim traces to a source file) · threshold from Rework: an objection in 3 or more losses updates the battle card
The rules of the loop
The AI proposes, a person merges
Automate the reading and the drafting. Keep the decision with whoever owns the file.
One owner per file
A name, not a team. The loop pings that person.
Never a silent write
The output is a proposed change, not an edited file.
Cite the source
Each proposed line carries the call and the quote.
Date and prune
Remove what no recent call supports.
The loop · When it runs
Give each file a trigger
Each closed deal
Competitors and proof: who won, why, what the buyer said.
Every Monday
Objections and “their words” from last week’s calls. Ten minutes.
Every month
Each owner rereads their file, prunes it and dates it.
Every quarter
Three wins and three losses, reread in full: ICP and positioning.
Guides do not agree on one cadence. Triggers drawn from GTMnow (Monday update, after every deal), Buffer in MKT1 (a monthly ping to each owner) and Rework (quarterly win-loss review)
The loop · How much to automate
Four levels. Start at zero
Level 0 · Manual
Paste and ask
Transcripts and files in one chat. Copy back what you accept.
Level 1 · Connected
The AI fetches
Connectors to your call recorder and CRM bring last week’s calls and deals.
Level 2 · Scheduled
It runs on Monday
A scheduled task does the same and leaves the proposal for you to review.
Level 3 · Pull request
It proposes in Git
A cloud agent opens a pull request on the repo. You read the diff and merge.
Get call text from the recorder’s own connector: the CRM sync usually carries the summary, not the transcript. Docs: Claude scheduled tasks · ChatGPT tasks · Claude Code cloud tasks · read Nov 2026
The loop · Does it work?
Keep a small test set
01
Pick five real tasks
A cold email, an objection reply, an ad, a competitor question, a call prep.
02
Save today’s answers
Same prompts, same accounts. That is your baseline.
03
Rerun after each update
Read old and new side by side: better, the same, or worse?
Anthropic: 20 to 50 simple tasks drawn from real failures is a great start · OpenAI: keep a golden set, read the outputs, let the domain experts own it. No GTM team has published a before-and-after test of a context update.
03

15 min

Done when one file changed, and you can point to the sentence in the call that caused it.

Outbound · The message
Short, no pitch, one proof
icp.md
The trigger, and the buyer’s own words
positioning.md

first email · 44 words
Subject: phone bookings
Saw you opened a third site in Laval.
Owners at that size tell us the phone becomes the bottleneck: “I spend my mornings confirming classes.”
A four-site studio near you moved bookings online in three weeks.
Worth a look at how they did it?
Gong, 28 million cold emails, July 2025: 100 words or fewer does best, and pitching cut replies by up to 57%. A vendor’s data, on its own customers.
Outbound · Where the AI fits
The AI researches, a person writes
4.1%
replies when the AI wrote it alone
The email nobody reread.
10.4%
replies when a person wrote it alone
Good, and slow.
14.7%
replies when the AI researched and a person wrote
The AI reads the files and the account. You write the forty words.
Saleshandy, June 2026: one vendor’s test on 12,000 prospects, with unequal groups and no significance test. The only measured comparison we found; read it as a direction.
Outbound · Before you press send
The rules of the channel
Prove who you are
SPF, DKIM and DMARC set up on the domain you send from
Stay under 0.3%
Spam complaints. Offer a one-click unsubscribe
Send little
Tens of emails per mailbox per day, not hundreds
Canada
CASL: you need consent, express or implied, and you must be able to prove it
United States
CAN-SPAM: honest subject, postal address, a working opt-out
What to expect
Published reply rates run from under 1% to 9%. Measure your own
Headline facts, not legal advice. Sources: Google sender guidelines · Yahoo · Canada’s anti-spam legislation · FTC, CAN-SPAM · Smartlead benchmarks

Workato, lead response time study: a mystery shop of 114 B2B companies, published March 2026. A vendor study. The famous “five-minute” figures come from 2007 to 2011 data and have not been rerun.
Inbound · Reading the results
Judge an angle on your own number
We moved ours from leads to meetings held. Pick yours: the number closest to revenue that you can count every week.
After a few days
Is the hook working?
Do people stop and click? If not, fix the first line, not the angle.
After 2 to 4 weeks
Does the angle bring leads?
Cost per qualified lead. Do not swap the creative before then.
After one sales cycle
Did it move your number?
For us, meetings held. Only this result changes positioning.md.
The platforms want volume to learn: about 50 results per ad set per week on Meta and TikTok, 30 conversions over 30 days on Google. Most small B2B accounts never reach that, so read every verdict as a direction, not a proof.
Inbound · The same loop again
Results go back into the files
An ad result is a signal, like a call. It proposes a change. The file’s owner approves it.
1 · Launch
angles from the files
2 · Read
your number, by angle
3 · Decide
keep, fix or stop
4 · Write back
what won, and why
Weekly
Inbound · Automating the judgment
Write your judgment down once
At each step of the loop, ask three questions. The answers are a skill.
What do I look at?
The data
Spend, leads and your number, by angle, for which dates.
What do I do with it?
The analysis
Your own rules: when an angle is winning, tired or dead.
What do I know that it does not?
The context
The files, and the decisions you already made.
SKILL.md
The three answers, in one file

Reads, analyses, drafts the verdict

05
Exercise
20 min
One ad, one page
1
Ask for three angles, each from a different file: a pain, an objection, a proof.
2
Pick one. Write the ad and the top of the page: headline, one line, one proof, one button.
3
Swap test: put a competitor’s logo on it. Still true? Rewrite until it is not.
4
Five-second test: show the page to your neighbour, then hide it. What is it, and who is it for?
Done when the ad and the page say the same sentence, and your neighbour can repeat it.

Live teardown
Five questions we ask of any layer
One volunteer shares their folder. The room reviews it with these.
Who is it for?
Would a stranger know after one read, and know who it is not for?
Says who?
Does each claim name the call, deal or doc behind it?
Only you?
Put a competitor’s name on it. Is the line still true?
Where do you lose?
Is there one honest line about a deal you lost?
Still true?
Is there a date and a name? What changed after the last five calls?
Group discussion · 15 minutes

4
What is the first thing you will do with this on Monday?
Two minutes with your neighbour first, then the room.
